hyps.why: Without edge 4 the output relies more on the node-2 path, so a strong conv on edge 5 matters more.
Replacing the key output-edge conv with parameter-free pooling loses much more than replacing none or skip.
If node 1 receives no input, a conv on its outgoing edge contributes almost nothing.
A conv from an empty node 1 is wasted.
With edge 4 removed, node 1 features reach the output only indirectly via edge 2, reducing the value of a conv into node 1.
If node 2 has no outgoing edge, computation into node 2 never reaches the output.
Deleting an existing 3x3 conv hurts far more than deleting a skip, pool or empty edge.
Removing the direct input-output edge when edge 5 is already absent leaves few or no paths into the output.
Adding a residual where none existed helps, whereas replacing a conv with skip tends to lose accuracy.
Stacking two 3x3 convs forms a deeper path with a larger receptive field, which NAS-Bench-201 rewards.
